scope: Finite47 covered unclassified examples only. Nearest centreline/source branch observations distinguish separate parallel bridge carriageways from a common-source-node pavement. No layer ordinal is used as absolute height, no whole-pair coupling/headroom rule is proposed.
conclusion: The finite observed branches are distinct, oppositely directed parallel one-way ribbons with active source bridge flags. They have no shared full connector or retained OSM route identity. Planar overlap and equal relative layer do not establish one physical deck or an ordered crossing. A separately source-bound paired-carriageway/facility identity and exact finite ribbon classification are still needed before any new co-elevation or headroom equation.
remainingGaps: Nearest source branch geometry is an observation, not an actual Surface binding or permission to merge the ribbons.
No shared connector/route/facility relation in held V11 proves both bridge sheets are one deck.
The same pair has other missing-historical-coverage samples with old/current gaps up to6.8m; no whole-pair or whole-level exemption is safe.
A bridge-existence metric lower floor above terrain/water remains independently required for any proposed positive height-domain release.
